topic: Discovery stories / peptides your body makes: TRH (thyrotropin-releasing hormone), the brain's 3-amino-acid thyroid switch, found by processing millions of sheep and pig hypothalamic fragments. Guillemin worked with 5 million hypothalamic fragments from sheep, Schally with the same amount from pigs; after years they had 1 mg of pure substance that released TSH from the pituitary; structure a three-amino-acid peptide (Nobel Prize 1977 press release, nobelprize.org); Guillemin isolated TRF/TRH in 1969, a simple tripeptide processed from a large precursor (Rivier, Hunter & Evans, PNAS 2024); TRH made in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus, stimulates TSH (and prolactin) (Society for Endocrinology, You and Your Hormones); TSH stimulates thyroid T4/T3; increased free T4 and T3 inhibit release of TRH and TSH by negative feedback (Shahid et al., StatPearls 'Physiology, Thyroid Hormone' 2023); Nobel 1977 to Guillemin and Schally 'for their discoveries concerning the peptide hormone production of the brain'
